# clean_game_json_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Tidy every game JSON file: sort its keys and drop empty values.

## Synopsis

```
clean_game_json_files [options]
```

## Description

Rewrites each game JSON file in the metadata repository, across all supercategories,
categories and subcategories, with keys sorted and four-space indentation.

Top-level keys whose value is null, an empty string, an empty list or object, or
`false` are removed. Nested values are left as they are.

## Options

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Clean every JSON file

```bash
clean_game_json_files
```

### Clean without the confirmation prompt

```bash
clean_game_json_files --no-preview
```

### Show which files would be cleaned

```bash
clean_game_json_files -p -v
```

## Notes

- There are no selection options; every JSON file is processed.
- A key set to `false` is removed, so a false flag and a missing flag end up the same.
